options: The on-prem tool (formerly Azure AD Connect) that synchronizes objects from on-prem AD to Entra ID
A replacement for Active Directory that removes the need for domain controllers
questions.explain: Entra Connect is installed on-prem and acts as the bridge, reading from AD and writing matching objects into Entra ID.

questions.q: By default, how often does an Entra Connect delta sync cycle run?
options: Only when an administrator manually triggers it
questions.explain: The default scheduled sync cycle interval is 30 minutes, though it can be triggered manually sooner.

questions.q: Which PowerShell cmdlet forces an immediate delta sync cycle?
questions.explain: Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta runs a delta sync immediately instead of waiting for the next scheduled run.

questions.q: In the default Entra Connect configuration, which direction does core object synchronization flow?
options: One-way, from on-prem AD to Entra ID
One-way, from Entra ID to on-prem AD
questions.explain: Core sync is one-way from on-prem AD to Entra ID; on-prem AD remains the authoritative source.

questions.q: What does password writeback let a user do?
options: Reset their password via Entra ID self-service and have that new password flow back to on-prem AD
Change their on-prem AD username from the Entra ID portal
Bypass Entra Connect's sync schedule entirely
questions.explain: Password writeback is an opt-in feature that flows a self-service password reset back down to on-prem AD.
